Fixed in 7ed2ef001. The client loop now holds an `active_session` id, set on every successful `session/new` reply, and the notification handler drops updates whose `session_id` doesn't match before touching `context_size`, mode, or the desktop notification callback.

Updates arriving before any session exists can't be attributed to a superseded session, so those are still accepted — that's the pre-first-session case, not a stale one. Lock poisoning also fails open, since dropping real updates is worse than accepting a stale one.

Worth noting the latch is complete on this branch because `NewSession` is the only session-creating request here; there's no `session/load` path on `main` to also cover.

Test: `updates_for_a_superseded_session_are_ignored`.

You're right — `spawn_client_loop` uses `std::thread::spawn` with its own current-thread runtime, so dropping the `start()` future can't abort it, and `handle_requests` awaited `initialize` (and `session/new`) with no bound and no select on `rx` closure. The `Child` is held by `run_with_child` on that thread, so a wedged handshake pinned the adapter process indefinitely.

Fixed in 10df531 by putting the cancellation where the child actually lives rather than at the caller: both startup requests are now wrapped in `tokio::time::timeout(STARTUP_TIMEOUT /* 60s */, …)`. On elapse `initialize` returns an error out of `connect_with`, which unwinds to `run_with_child`'s `child.kill().await` / `child.wait().await` and ends the thread; `session/new` reports the timeout to its `response_tx` so the loop stays responsive and unwinds when `start()` drops `tx`. `spawn_acp_process` already sets `kill_on_drop(true)`, so the child is reaped either way. 60s is a wedge backstop for a cold adapter start, not a latency budget — the 10s RPC bound and 4s desktop bound still govern picker responsiveness.

Correct — I bounded `session/new` itself but left `apply_session_config_options` and `apply_session_mode` outside the deadline, so an adapter that answered `session/new` and then wedged on `session/set-config-option` or `session/set-mode` still pinned its child.

Fixed in ead0dd0. The whole startup exchange now runs inside a single `tokio::time::timeout(STARTUP_TIMEOUT, …)` — `session/new`, the config options, and the mode application — rather than one timeout per request, so the bound is on total startup rather than per-hop. `session_ids.push` stays immediately after `session/new` so a session that fails during setup is still tracked for close.

One behavior change worth calling out: `apply_session_config_options(...).await?` previously propagated out of `handle_requests` and tore down the client loop. It's now reported through `response_tx` like the mode path. Net effect is the same — `start()` gets the error and drops `tx`, which unwinds the loop — but the failure is now attributable to the caller instead of surfacing as a bare loop exit.

`cargo clippy -p goose --all-targets` clean; `acp::` lib tests (197) and the `acp_provider_test` integration suite, which drives this exact startup path over a real transport, both pass.

discussion_comments.comment_body: 🤖 Addressed in 8d59f22ec. Both model changes and provider config changes now call `reset_provider_notification_task` immediately after provider recreation. That aborts and clears the old receiver task, so the next prompt subscribes to the newly created provider instead of waiting on the stale provider receiver. Added focused coverage for aborting/clearing the task slot.

🤖 Addressed in d536a6cdc. Every ordered prompt-channel send now uses awaited `send()` instead of lossy `try_send`, including text/thought, tool start/completion, terminal metadata, permission requests, and final prompt success/error. The active sender is cloned before awaiting, so no synchronous mutex guard is held across suspension. The fake nested ACP agent now emits 128 terminal deltas (2× channel capacity); the regression requires all sequence numbers in order, terminal exit, tool completion, and final prompt stream termination within 5 seconds. Focused test, full ACP provider suite (14 passed/9 ignored), ACP unit suite (202 passed), and clippy all pass locally.

Good catch — confirmed. `goose-cli`'s `process_agent_response` `drop(stream)`s on Ctrl-C (`session/mod.rs:1405`), so the in-poll dispatch never ran on that path and no `session/cancel` was sent.

Fixed in 56e5fdc: the provider `cancel()` dispatch now lives in a detached `CancelForwarder` task spawned at reply setup that fires on token cancellation, independent of the stream lifecycle — so it runs even when the consumer drops the stream. A drop-guard aborts the forwarder on normal (non-cancelled) completion so a normal turn doesn't leave a task waiting on a token that never fires. The reply loop still `break`s promptly on cancel so polling consumers (the ACP server) unblock without waiting for the backend to ack. Added `cancellation_forwards_to_provider_even_when_stream_is_dropped` covering the drop path.

**Fixed in 2e500c20.** `DeveloperClient::call_tool` now passes `cancel_token` to `shell_with_cwd`, which threads it through to `run_command`. The command wait now selects on the token alongside the existing timeout and kills the child process on cancellation, so a nested `developer.shell` awaiting a long-running command is terminated when the outer code-mode execution times out or is cancelled. Added `shell_kills_child_on_cancellation` covering this path.
